project: Fully Analog ECG Classifier on SKY130 ReRAM Crossbar
scope: Complete system: frontend feature extraction + MLP classifier on 1T1R crossbar + WTA output

summary.verdict: NOT PUBLISHABLE in current state. One fatal finding (WTA non-functional) invalidates the end-to-end analog claim. Nine major findings require significant additional work. Target venue after remediation: TBCAS or BioCAS conference, with JSSC requiring corners + layout.
summary.headline: The effective-weight mathematical pipeline (94.92%) is verified correct, but the actual SPICE netlist that implements it does not work. The 94.92% accuracy is a SOFTWARE number computed using weights extracted from individual crossbar unit-cell simulations — the full top-level circuit simulation fails completely.

findings.claim_attacked: Fully analog end-to-end classification achieving 94.92% accuracy
findings.finding: The top-level classifier netlist (top_level_classifier_circuit.spice) does NOT produce valid classifications. All 5 WTA outputs saturate to 1.788V (near VDD=1.8V) for every input beat. The WTA is not discriminating — it outputs the same voltage for all classes regardless of input.
findings.evidence: verify_circuit_classifier.py ngspice spot-check results: Beat 22597 (N): vout=[1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788]. Beat 41222 (S): vout=[1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788]. Beat 31504 (V): vout=[1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788]. Beat 25759 (F): vout=[1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788]. Beat 6191 (Q): vout=[1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788, 1.788]. Only 1/5 correct (the N beat, by coincidence). Saved in circuit_verification_results.json.
findings.impact: The claimed 94.92% full-analog accuracy is NOT from end-to-end SPICE simulation. It is from a mathematical pipeline: (1) simulate individual crossbar unit-cells to extract effective weights, (2) run numpy matrix multiplication with those weights. The actual circuit netlist fails completely. The '94.92% full analog' label is misleading — it should be '94.92% effective-weight accuracy' or '94.92% behavioral model accuracy'.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The authors claim 94.92% accuracy from a 'fully analog' classifier, but their own SPICE simulation of the complete netlist produces identical outputs for all inputs. The reported accuracy comes from a mathematical abstraction of the circuit, not from the circuit itself. This is a fundamental disconnect that invalidates the core contribution.
findings.remediation: Debug the top-level netlist: (1) The WTA inputs may be current-starved or voltage-saturated. Check that L2 crossbar outputs drive sufficient differential current into the WTA. (2) The CCCS-based MAC summation may not interface correctly with the interstage bias mirrors. (3) The .op analysis may be insufficient — try .tran with ramped inputs. (4) WTA transistor sizing (W=2u L=0.5u) may be wrong for the current levels involved. Effort: 2-4 weeks of circuit debugging.
findings.precedent: Multiple papers retracted or rejected for claiming simulation-verified accuracy when the actual simulation did not converge or produce correct results.

findings.claim_attacked: Circuit performance validated with SKY130 PDK models
findings.finding: All simulations use only the tt (typical-typical) process corner. No slow-slow (ss), fast-fast (ff), or cross-corners (sf/fs) have been simulated. No temperature variation (-40/27/85°C) or voltage variation (VDD±10%) analysis exists.
findings.evidence: Every .include in the project references only *__tt.corner.spice files. Grep for 'ss.corner|ff.corner|sf.corner|fs.corner' returns zero matches across the entire project. No .temp statements found in any classifier netlist.
findings.impact: ALL performance numbers are typical-only. Subthreshold circuits are exponentially sensitive to process variation — a 10mV Vth shift changes drain current by ~50% at room temperature. Without corners, the design may fail completely at ss corner or elevated temperature. No journal will accept typical-only results for a subthreshold analog design.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The entire design operates in subthreshold where drain current scales as exp(Vgs/nVT). Claiming validated performance without PVT corner analysis is unacceptable. At minimum, show ss/tt/ff corners at -40/27/85°C with VDD±10%.
findings.remediation: Run all critical circuits (frontend diff pairs, interstage bias mirrors, WTA, crossbar access transistors) across ss/tt/ff × {-40, 27, 85°C} × {0.81, 0.9, 0.99V for frontend; 1.62, 1.8, 1.98V for classifier}. Report accuracy degradation at worst-case corner. Effort: 1-2 weeks.
findings.precedent: Standard requirement for all analog IC publications (JSSC, TCAS, TBCAS).

findings.claim_attacked: Circuit performance validated with SKY130 PDK models
findings.finding: No Monte Carlo or statistical mismatch analysis has been performed. The mismatch corner files are included (.mismatch.corner.spice) but the _diff parameters for PFETs are all set to zero, effectively disabling PFET mismatch. No .mc analysis commands exist in any testbench.
findings.evidence: WTA_5class.spice lines 33-68: all sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8__*_diff parameters set to 0. Same in interstage_bias_relu.spice lines 14-48 and generate_top_level.py lines 21-29. Grep for '.mc|monte.carlo|agauss' in testbenches returns no matches (only in cap_mim model files).
findings.impact: Current mirrors, differential pairs, and the WTA all depend on matched transistor pairs. Without mismatch analysis, there is no evidence the design works with realistic device variation. The WTA is particularly sensitive — Lazzaro WTA with mismatched transistors will have a dead zone where it cannot discriminate close inputs.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The PFET mismatch parameters are explicitly zeroed out, disabling the mismatch model the PDK provides. Without Monte Carlo analysis showing yield under realistic mismatch, the circuit results are optimistic to the point of being misleading.
findings.remediation: Remove the _diff=0 overrides (use PDK default mismatch parameters). Run 200+ Monte Carlo iterations on the WTA, interstage, and frontend diff pairs. Report yield (percentage meeting accuracy threshold). Effort: 1-2 weeks.
findings.precedent: JSSC requires mismatch analysis for all current-mirror and differential-pair circuits.

findings.finding: The top-level classifier netlist contains 148 ideal SPICE elements: 8 VCVS (E-elements) for input conditioning and ~140 CCCS (F-elements) for MAC current summation. The VCVS elements model analog normalization (gain + offset) that would require real op-amps or resistive-feedback amplifiers in silicon. The CCCS elements model current transfer that occurs naturally in a physical crossbar (Kirchhoff's current law) — these are physically justified but the VCVS are not.
findings.evidence: top_level_classifier_circuit.spice lines 89-117: 8 Econd* VCVS elements with computed gain and offset. Lines 2308+: ~140 Fmac* CCCS elements. generate_top_level.py line 59 comment: 'For ASIC: each channel is a differential amplifier with resistive feedback... Modeled here as VCVS (E-element).'
findings.impact: The 8 input conditioning VCVS are NOT physical circuits — they are ideal behavioral models. In silicon, these would require 8 differential amplifiers or programmable gain stages, adding significant area and power. The design team acknowledges this in comments but has not designed the actual circuits. The CCCS elements for MAC are physically justified (column current summation in a crossbar).
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The input conditioning stage uses ideal voltage-controlled voltage sources. What are the actual circuits? What is their gain error, bandwidth, noise, and power consumption? Without these, the 'fully analog' claim is premature — a critical analog block is missing.
findings.remediation: Design 8 analog normalization circuits (diff amp with resistive feedback, or switchable-gain amplifier). Simulate with PVT corners. Add their power to the energy budget. Alternatively, acknowledge this as a missing block and provide a power estimate. Effort: 2-3 weeks for circuit design, or 1 day for honest acknowledgment.
findings.precedent: Common criticism of behavioral SPICE models in analog IC papers.

findings.finding: No physical layout has been created. No parasitic extraction (PEX) has been performed. All simulations are schematic-level only.
findings.evidence: No .spef, .gds, .mag, .lef, or layout-related files found in the project. No parasitic capacitance or resistance annotations in any netlist.
findings.impact: For a crossbar with 1,664 1T1R cells plus 69 interstage transistors and WTA, routing parasitics (especially column capacitance and IR drop) can significantly affect accuracy. Column parasitic capacitance in a crossbar slows settling and adds noise. IR drop on long bitlines creates systematic errors.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: Schematic-level simulation of a 1,664-cell crossbar array without parasitic extraction is insufficient. At minimum, estimate column parasitic capacitance and IR drop, and show they do not degrade accuracy beyond the reported margin.
findings.remediation: Either: (1) Create layout in Magic/KLayout and extract parasitics, or (2) estimate parasitics from crossbar geometry and add lumped RC models to the netlist. Effort: 2-4 weeks for layout, or 2-3 days for analytical estimates.
findings.precedent: All JSSC and most TCAS papers require post-layout simulation.

findings.finding: No energy measurement from SPICE simulation exists for the classifier. The energy numbers in mlp_sweep_results.json are from hand calculations (e_nj field), not from .measure statements on actual netlists. The ngspice_frontend_validation_guide.md describes how to measure energy but this was never executed on the final system.
findings.evidence: No .measure statements in any classifier netlist. mlp_sweep_results.json energy values (0.16-4.0 nJ) are computed analytically. The top-level classifier netlist uses .op (DC operating point), not .tran, so transient energy cannot be measured. The frontend has energy measurement scripts but they were not run on the complete system.
findings.impact: The GOALS.md target of <100 nJ/classification has no simulation evidence. The analytical estimates may be significantly wrong because they don't account for: (1) input conditioning amplifier power (VCVS is zero power), (2) settling time and dynamic power, (3) WTA competition energy, (4) crossbar sneak paths. The actual energy could easily be 10-100x higher than estimated.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The energy claim is entirely from hand calculation, not simulation. For a paper whose primary contribution is 'ultra-low-power analog classification,' the absence of simulated energy measurements is a critical omission.
findings.remediation: Run .tran simulation of the full classifier with realistic input waveforms. Use .measure to integrate VDD supply current over a classification period. Report per-block energy breakdown. Effort: 1-2 weeks (requires fixing JR-001 first).
findings.precedent: Liu et al. JSSC 2025 reports measured energy from silicon. Simulation-only papers at TBCAS still require .tran-based energy measurement.

findings.claim_attacked: ReRAM crossbar implements trained MLP weights
findings.finding: ReRAM devices are modeled as fixed resistors (R-elements) in the classifier netlist. No ReRAM variability, read disturb, or conductance drift is modeled. The SKY130 ReRAM PDK is present in the repository but its behavioral model is NOT used in any classifier simulation.
findings.evidence: top_level_classifier_circuit.spice line 124: 'Rrpl1_0_0 mpl1_0_0 cpl1_0 3378378.3784' — this is a fixed resistor, not a ReRAM model. Glob for 'skywater-pdk-libs-sky130_fd_pr_reram/models/*.spice' returns no files. No reference to ReRAM model in top_level_classifier_circuit.spice.
findings.impact: The 'foundry ReRAM PDK' novelty claim is weakened if the actual ReRAM model is not used in simulations. Real ReRAM devices have: (1) cycle-to-cycle variability (σ/μ ~5-20%), (2) device-to-device variability, (3) read disturb at repeated V_READ, (4) conductance drift over time. None of these are modeled. The 94.92% accuracy may degrade significantly under realistic ReRAM variation.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The authors claim to use the SKY130 ReRAM PDK, but the crossbar uses ideal fixed resistors. Where is the ReRAM device model? What is the accuracy under realistic conductance variation (±10% device-to-device, ±5% cycle-to-cycle)? Without this, the crossbar is indistinguishable from an ideal resistive array.
findings.remediation: Either: (1) Use the SKY130 ReRAM behavioral model for crossbar simulation, or (2) run Monte Carlo with Gaussian variation on each resistance value (σ = 5-20% of mean). Report accuracy vs. variability level. Effort: 1-3 days for Monte Carlo on resistors, 1-2 weeks for full ReRAM model integration.
findings.precedent: Multiple ReRAM crossbar papers require variability-aware training or report accuracy vs. conductance variation.

findings.finding: The headline 94.92% accuracy is the BEST of 10 random seeds (seed 47), not the expected accuracy. The mean across 10 seeds is 94.49% ± 0.30%. The full_analog_accuracy is computed only for seed 47.
findings.evidence: circuit_retrain_results.json: best_seed=47, sw_accuracy=94.749 (best of [94.23, 94.68, 93.77, 94.58, 94.68, 94.75, 94.65, 94.25, 94.73, 94.62]). full_analog_accuracy=94.921% computed only for seed 47 weights. INTEGRATION_HANDOFF.md more honestly reports 94.44±0.29% (the mean).
findings.impact: Reporting best-of-10 inflates accuracy by ~0.26-0.47pp over expected mean. While the inflation is modest, it is methodologically incorrect. A reviewer will note this immediately.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The reported 94.92% is the maximum of 10 random seeds. Report mean ± standard deviation (94.49 ± 0.30%) as the primary result. Computing the full-analog accuracy only for the best seed introduces selection bias into the primary metric.
findings.remediation: Compute full_analog_accuracy for all 10 seeds and report mean ± std. Effort: 1 hour (just re-run the effective-weight pipeline for each seed).
findings.precedent: Standard practice in ML — reporting best-of-N without disclosure is considered cherry-picking.

findings.finding: The N class constitutes 88.7% of the test set (42,692/48,139 beats). A trivial majority-class classifier achieves 88.7% accuracy. The reported 94.92% is only 6.2 percentage points above this trivial baseline. Meanwhile, clinically important minority classes have poor recall: V=80.4%, F=51.0%, Q=0.0%.
findings.evidence: circuit_verification_results.json confusion matrix: N support=42692 (88.7%). V recall=80.4% (2585/3216). F recall=51.0% (198/388). Q recall=0.0% (0/7). Macro-average F1=0.61.
findings.impact: Overall accuracy is a misleading metric here. The system misclassifies 19.6% of ventricular beats (V) and 49% of fusion beats (F). For a cardiac monitoring device, missing ventricular ectopy is a safety concern. The macro-average F1 of 0.61 is a more honest summary.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: Overall accuracy of 94.9% on a dataset with 88.7% majority class is not informative. Report balanced accuracy, macro-F1, and per-class sensitivity/specificity. The 80.4% V sensitivity is concerning for a cardiac monitoring application. How does this compare to clinical requirements (ANSI/AAMI EC57)?
findings.remediation: Report balanced accuracy and macro-F1 as primary metrics alongside overall accuracy. Contextualize V recall relative to clinical requirements. Consider class-weighted loss during training. Effort: 1-2 days for retraining with class weights, 1 hour for reporting balanced metrics.
findings.precedent: De Chazal et al. (2004) original paper reports per-class metrics. All AAMI-compliant studies report Se+ and +P per class.

findings.finding: The V (ventricular) recall for the best seed (47) is 80.4%, missing the project's own target of >=90% by nearly 10 percentage points. The mean V recall across seeds (from full_validation.py) is 86.3±3.0% — still below the 90% target at every seed.
findings.evidence: GOALS.md line 8: 'V sensitivity (ventricular): >= 90%'. circuit_verification_results.json: V recall=80.4% (2585/3216) for seed 47. INTEGRATION_HANDOFF.md reports V_sensitivity=86.3%. Both are below 90%.
findings.impact: The project fails its own stated target for the most clinically important metric (ventricular beat sensitivity). This is not acknowledged in any report or handoff document.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: The authors' own specification requires >=90% V sensitivity. The best result achieves 80.4% (or 86.3% averaged). This 10pp shortfall in the most safety-critical metric must be acknowledged and explained.
findings.remediation: Either: (1) Improve V recall through class-weighted training, threshold adjustment, or architecture changes, or (2) Acknowledge the shortfall and revise the target with justification. Effort: variable (retraining may not close 10pp gap without larger model).
findings.precedent: AAMI EC57 standard for automated arrhythmia detection.

findings.finding: The MLP hyperparameters (hidden=64, lr=1e-3, alpha=1e-4, batch=128) are identical across all scripts with no hyperparameter search script that uses DS2 accuracy as objective. diag_hyperparams.py exists but is for SNN, not MLP. If these were informally tuned by checking DS2 accuracy, that constitutes implicit data leakage.
findings.evidence: Grep shows identical hyperparams in retrain_circuit_features.py and generate_circuit_feature_cache.py. No hyperparameter search script for MLP found. diag_hyperparams.py targets SNN architecture.
findings.impact: Unknown magnitude. If hyperparams were tuned on DS2, the reported accuracy is optimistically biased. However, there is no direct evidence of leakage — the parameters may have been chosen a priori or from literature.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: How were the MLP hyperparameters selected? Was any hyperparameter tuning performed using the test set? If so, report nested cross-validation accuracy.
findings.remediation: Document the hyperparameter selection process. If DS2 was used, run nested CV. Effort: 1 day.
findings.precedent: Common methodology critique in ML papers.

findings.finding: Features are extracted as float32 (generate_circuit_feature_cache.py line 94: dtype=np.float32) but StandardScaler and MLPClassifier operate on float64. Silent promotion occurs.
findings.evidence: generate_circuit_feature_cache.py line 94: feat = np.zeros(8, dtype=np.float32). sklearn StandardScaler internally uses float64.
findings.impact: Unlikely to affect accuracy by more than ~0.01pp. Features have ~7 decimal digits of precision. However, results may differ slightly across platforms or numpy versions that handle the promotion differently.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: Minor: ensure consistent floating-point precision throughout the pipeline for reproducibility.
findings.remediation: Use float64 throughout, or explicitly cast to float64 before scaler. Effort: 5 minutes.

findings.finding: Per-class confidence intervals are not reported. The 10-seed analysis gives overall CI, but per-class recalls have much wider variance: S=69.2±6.7%, V=86.3±3.0%. The circuit_retrain_results.json only has per_class_f1 for seed 47.
findings.evidence: INTEGRATION_HANDOFF.md reports S=69.2±6.7%, V=86.3±3.0% (wide CIs). circuit_retrain_results.json has per_class_f1 only for one seed.
findings.impact: The S-class recall 95% CI spans [55.8%, 82.6%] — a range so wide that the true S-class performance is highly uncertain.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: Report per-class sensitivity confidence intervals. The S-class CI of ±6.7% indicates the classifier may achieve anywhere from 56% to 83% S sensitivity depending on the random seed.
findings.remediation: Report per_class_f1 and recall for all 10 seeds with mean ± std. Effort: 30 minutes.

findings.finding: Frontend testbenches use extensive .ic statements for EWMA, timer, and sample-and-hold initial conditions. In silicon, these initial conditions would require a startup/calibration circuit that does not exist in the design.
findings.evidence: Frontend testbenches (_acc_101_b16.spice, etc.) contain 8+ .ic statements per testbench: .ic V(xrr.net_timer)=0.9, .ic V(xrr.ewma_node)=0.371658, etc. bias_gen.spice line 38: 'Startup: use .ic v(xbias.iref)=0.3 in testbench with uic'.
findings.impact: The EWMA charge-sharing circuit requires IC calibration (V_sf = 0.480 - 0.176*RR per memory). Without a startup circuit, the EWMA will take many heartbeats to converge from an arbitrary initial state, producing wrong F1/F2 features during warmup.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: How does the EWMA initialize in silicon? The simulation uses .ic statements that are not realizable in hardware. A startup circuit or convergence analysis is needed.
findings.remediation: Either: (1) Design a startup circuit that precharges EWMA to nominal value, or (2) Show convergence analysis — how many beats until features are valid after power-on? Effort: 2-3 days.

findings.finding: Report balanced accuracy and macro-F1 as primary metrics alongside overall accuracy. The current reporting emphasizes overall accuracy (94.92%) which is inflated by the 88.7% majority class.
findings.evidence: Macro-average F1 = 0.61 (from verification results). Balanced accuracy ≈ (97.0 + 82.7 + 80.4 + 51.0 + 0.0) / 5 = 62.2%.
findings.impact: Would provide honest assessment of system capability.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: Add balanced accuracy and macro-F1 to the results table.
findings.remediation: Add two numbers to the results table. Effort: 5 minutes.
findings.precedent: Best practice per sklearn documentation and AAMI EC57.

findings.finding: DS2 record 123 is missing from the evaluation (21 records instead of 22). This record was dropped due to missing annotations in the cache but is part of the standard DS2 split.
findings.evidence: generate_circuit_feature_cache.py processes 21 DS2 records. Record 123 is absent. full_validation.py previously addressed this but the cache was not regenerated.
findings.impact: Removing one record from the test set slightly changes the accuracy (likely <0.1pp). The record should be included for completeness.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: Why is DS2 record 123 excluded? This should be noted explicitly.
findings.remediation: Either include record 123 or add a footnote explaining its exclusion. Effort: 1 hour.
findings.precedent: Inter-patient protocol requires all records in each set.

findings.finding: The frontend and classifier have never been simulated together in SPICE. The frontend produces analog voltages; the classifier takes analog voltages as input. But no testbench connects frontend_top.spice outputs to the classifier's feature inputs.
findings.evidence: No SPICE file connects frontend_top.spice subcircuit to top_level_classifier_circuit.spice. The verify_circuit_classifier.py uses numpy-computed features as direct voltage inputs via the script (not SPICE frontend outputs).
findings.impact: Analog interfaces may have level-shifting, loading, or settling issues that only appear when the stages are connected. This gap means the 'end-to-end' claim covers ECG→features (frontend SPICE) and features→class (classifier SPICE/math) separately, but never ECG→features→class in one simulation.
findings.what_a_reviewer_would_say: Has the full chain been simulated as one piece? Show at least one beat classification starting from an ECG waveform input to the frontend and ending at the WTA output.
findings.remediation: Create a combined testbench that feeds ECG PWL into the frontend and connects frontend outputs to the classifier input conditioning. Effort: 1-2 weeks (requires fixing JR-001 first).

gaps_added_to_skill: Float32/float64 consistency check (found float32→float64 silent promotion)
StandardScaler leakage check (verified clean — fit on DS1 only)
ReRAM model fidelity check (found fixed resistors instead of ReRAM behavioral model)
PFET mismatch parameter override check (found all _diff params zeroed)
Full-chain end-to-end SPICE simulation existence check
clean_checks: StandardScaler fitted on DS1 only — no data leakage (generate_circuit_feature_cache.py lines 125-127, retrain_circuit_features.py lines 222-228)
No feature uses future information — corrected extractor does not use post_rr (generate_circuit_feature_cache.py has zero post_rr references)
EWMA temporal causality correct — ewma_before captures pre-update value, matches circuit charge-share timing
Weight mapping mathematically verified to machine epsilon (retrain_circuit_features.py map_weights_to_conductance())
De Chazal inter-patient protocol correctly implemented (DS1=22 records train, DS2=21 records test)
Feature ordering consistent across all scripts: [F1_rr_dev, F4_bi_L1, F2_rr_asym, F5_pwave, F6_width, F3_bi_L0, F7_slope, F8_rpeak]
All frontend circuits use only SKY130 PDK transistors (no ideal devices in frontend)
Hybrid mirror+diode load topology correctly implemented in all diff pairs (prevents bistability)
Offset-binary encoding correctly converts signed normalized features to positive voltages
